title: a native pin may be applied to an async function: `native(fn)` is an assertion over a graph, not a call, so it starts no work and an async function is not rejected merely for needing runtime support
notes: Obligation: specification/compatibility.mdx, 'Native and Wasm Targets': 'Closures, classes, generics, unions, and async functions MUST NOT be rejected solely because runtime support is required.' Same page, 'Native Pin': 'A native pin MUST be a checked assertion over the complete transitive graph. Compilation MUST fail if any reachable operation or provider requires TypeScript' — nothing `scale` reaches requires TypeScript, so the pin has no ground to fail on. docs/DECISIONS.md 'Concurrency' (Locked) scopes the rule the reference used to apply here to work that was STARTED: 'Fire-and-forget and detached work are initially unavailable in authored .sm. Every started Promise must be consumed by await or by a recognized combinator'; specification/requirements.mdx, 'Scoping' repeats it as 'every STARTED Promise MUST be consumed'. Passing a function reference to a compiler-owned assertion starts nothing. Written from the specification before it was run. The counterpart positive case a-clean-graph-satisfies-the-pin is the same program with `async` removed and passes on both backends, which isolates `async` as the whole difference. The `js` xfail here is RETIRED: poc/src/language/semantic.ts's callback-ownership pass treated every function-valued argument as a callback, so `native(asyncFn)` drew `SMITHERS1404` and the pin was inapplicable to every async function. The pass now recognizes the `smithers:native` intrinsic — by checker symbol identity against the compiler-owned prelude, so a locally declared `native` still owns nothing — and exempts its pinned argument from the started-Promise rule.
